answer: Not necessarily. The 3-minute SLA is the first gate: a record-at-a-time path is only needed when no trigger fits under the SLA (the latency floor is the trigger plus the run). A micro-batch with about a 30 second trigger (p99 around 40 seconds) meets a 3-minute SLA comfortably. Second, when both engines meet the SLA, the team decides: since ops already runs the batch cluster, a micro-batch stream on that same cluster (same code, deploy pipeline, on-call) is the choice, and a separate record-at-a-time runtime is not justified. Build record-at-a-time only if the SLA drops to about 1-2 seconds or the tail latency misses.
